topic.title: Plant hormones and phototropism
topic.subject: science
topic.examWeightHint: A short, reliable question on both tiers. Foundation asks three one-mark questions — name the process, name the hormone, state the direction — and Summer 2025 lost marks on all three. Higher adds the four-step mechanism of outcome 1.6.12, usually inside a tip experiment with three or four treatments, and is natural QWC material because the four bullets plus the two naming points give six indicative points on their own.
mustMemorise: Phototropism: the growth of a stem towards light
Auxin is produced at the TIP of the shoot
Light makes the auxin UNEVEN: more on the SHADED side
Auxin causes cell ELONGATION, so the shaded side grows longer and the shoot bends towards the light
No tip means no auxin, so no growth and no bending
notOnThisSpec: Other plant hormones: gibberellin, ethene, abscisic acid
Commercial uses of plant hormones: selective weedkillers, rooting powder, ripening fruit
The names of the scientists who did the classic tip experiments
How auxin acts on the cell wall at molecular level

State the direction of bending with the word 'towards the light'
Give the four Higher stages in order: made at the tip, moves down, uneven, elongation
Say which side the auxin collects on, and why that bends the shoot towards the light
Use the word elongation rather than 'more cells'
Say that a shoot with no tip neither bends nor grows

Explain why a clear cap is a control and why repeats improve reliability, not accuracy
sheet.howExamined: B1 Foundation (60 marks, 1 hour) and B1 Higher (70 marks, 1 hour), calculator allowed. Outcome 1.6.11 is common to both tiers; 1.6.12 is Higher only. Foundation questions are three one-mark recall parts attached to a diagram of a bending shoot. Higher questions set the mechanism inside a tip experiment with three to five treatments, often with a mean or a percentage to calculate, and the explanation carries [3]-[4]. The schemes are point-for-point and the names are strict: phototropism, auxin, shaded side, elongation.
traps: Naming the process photosynthesis instead of phototropism (Summer 2025 B1 F Q4)
Offering an animal hormone, or chlorophyll, instead of auxin (Summer 2025 B1 F Q4)
Answering 'it moves' or 'it grows differently' where a direction is needed (Summer 2025 B1 F Q4)
Putting the extra auxin on the lit side
Writing 'more cells' or 'the cells divide' instead of elongation
Saying only 'no tip, so no auxin' and never adding 'so it did not grow' (Summer 2025 B1 H Q4)
Leaving a diagram part-completed when the question says to complete it (Summer 2025 B1 H Q4)
Dividing a percentage increase by the final value instead of the original (March 2026 B1 H Q7)
Describing the plant as wanting or looking for the light

steps.working: Auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot.
steps.decision: Start where the specification starts. The first bullet of 1.6.12 is the site of production, and it is the cheapest mark in the question.

steps.working: The auxin moves down the shoot.
steps.decision: Second bullet. It is easy to skip because it feels obvious, but it is a separate marking point.

steps.working: The one-sided light makes the auxin unevenly distributed, with more on the shaded side.
steps.decision: Third bullet. Say which side: 'uneven' alone does not show you know the direction, and the direction is what the whole answer turns on.

steps.working: Auxin makes the cells elongate, so the shaded side grows longer than the lit side and the shoot curves towards the light.
steps.decision: Fourth bullet. The word is elongate. 'Grows more' is usually accepted but 'makes more cells' is not, because that is cell division, not elongation.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: Auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot and moves down it. The light coming from one side makes the auxin unevenly distributed, so there is more auxin on the shaded side than on the lit side. Auxin causes cells to elongate, so the cells on the shaded side become longer than those on the lit side and the shoot bends towards the light.

steps.working: Shoot A curved by 31° and shoot E, with the stem below the tip covered, still curved by 32°.
steps.decision: Quote the two figures that are almost the same. A comparison without numbers is the commonest way to lose an explanation mark on a data question.

steps.working: Shoot C, with the tip covered, curved by only 1°.
steps.decision: Now quote the odd one out. One treatment differs from the control by one change, and that change is the tip.

steps.working: Covering the stem makes no difference but covering the tip stops the bending, so the tip is the part that detects the light.
steps.decision: State the conclusion in the words the question asked for. The data are the evidence; the sentence is the mark.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: Shoot A curved by 31° and shoot E, whose stem below the tip was covered, still curved by 32°, so covering the stem makes almost no difference. Shoot C, whose tip was covered, curved by only 1°. The tip is therefore the part of the shoot that detects the light.

twin.stem: In the same investigation, shoot B had its tip cut off and curved by 0°, while shoot D had a clear cap over its tip and curved by 30°. Explain what this pair of results shows.

accepted: the shoot with a clear cap still curved, so the cap itself does not stop the bending, and the shoot with the tip cut off did not curve at all, so the tip is needed and it is the tip that produces the auxin

items.stem: A shoot grows towards a lamp placed to one side of it. What is this response called?

options.feedback: Phototropism: photo- for light, -tropism for a growth response. Summer 2025 Foundation examiners reported photosynthesis offered here instead.
Photosynthesis is how the plant makes glucose. The word you want shares the first four letters and nothing else: phototropism.
Transpiration is water loss from leaves. This question is about the direction the shoot grows.
Not a term CCEA uses. The growth of a stem towards light is phototropism.

items.stem: Which hormone causes a shoot to bend towards the light?

options.feedback: Auxin. It is the only plant hormone CCEA's B1 names, so it is the only one that can be the answer here.
Insulin is an animal hormone that lowers blood glucose. Summer 2025 examiners saw several animal hormones offered in this part.
Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light for photosynthesis, not a hormone.
ADH is the human hormone that makes the kidney reabsorb more water. The plant hormone here is auxin.

items.stem: A shoot is lit from the left only. Where does the auxin collect?
items.skill: Get the direction of the uneven distribution right

options.text: on the right side, away from the light
options.feedback: More auxin where there is less light. Those cells then elongate more and the shoot leans left, towards the lamp.

options.text: on the left side, facing the light
options.feedback: That would make the lit side grow longer and the shoot would lean away from the lamp, which is not what happens. Auxin collects on the shaded side.

options.text: at the tip only, never lower down
options.feedback: Auxin is made at the tip but moves down the shoot. The bending happens below the tip, where the cells elongate.
Even auxin gives even growth and a straight shoot. One-sided light makes the distribution uneven — that is the whole mechanism.

items.stem: What does auxin do to the cells on the shaded side of a shoot?

options.feedback: Elongate — they get longer. A row of longer cells on one side forces the shoot to curve.

options.text: it makes them divide more often
options.feedback: More cells is cell division. The specification's word is elongation: the same cells become longer.
The shaded side receives less light, so it cannot be photosynthesising faster. Auxin acts on cell length.
Shrinking on the shaded side would bend the shoot away from the light. Auxin lengthens cells.

items.stem: The tip is cut off a young shoot, which is then lit from one side. What happens?
items.skill: Say the consequence, not just the cause

options.text: it does not grow and does not bend
options.feedback: Both halves of the answer. Summer 2025 Higher examiners reported that most candidates said there was no tip or no auxin but fewer said there was no growth.

options.text: it grows straight up but does not bend
options.feedback: The tip is the source of the auxin that makes cells elongate, so removing it stops the growth as well as the bending.

options.text: it bends towards the light as usual
options.feedback: With no tip there is no auxin, so there is nothing to make one side elongate.

options.text: it bends away from the light
options.feedback: Nothing makes a shoot bend away from light on this specification. With the tip gone, the shoot does neither.

items.stem: Which of these is a full-mark answer to 'State what the shoot will do'?
items.skill: Give a direction, not an impression

options.text: The shoot bends towards the light.
options.feedback: A direction and the thing it bends towards. That is what the mark scheme wants.

options.text: The shoot looks for the light.
options.feedback: A plant cannot look for anything. Describe the growth: the shoot bends towards the light.
Too vague to score. Summer 2025 Foundation examiners described exactly this kind of answer. Say which way it bends.
'Differently' names no direction. Differential growth is the explanation; bending towards the light is the observation.

parts.stem:
A young shoot is grown in a closed box with a single slit cut in the left-hand side, so light reaches it from the left only.
Explain, using auxin, why the shoot bends to the left.

accepted: auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot and moves down the shoot, the light from the left makes the auxin uneven so there is more auxin on the shaded right side, auxin makes those cells elongate so the right side grows longer and the shoot bends to the left towards the light

scheme.for: auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot
auxin moves down the shoot
light causes an uneven distribution: more auxin on the shaded (right) side
reject: more auxin on the lit side

scheme.for: auxin causes the cells on that side to elongate, so that side grows longer and the shoot bends towards the light

hints: Four bullets in the specification, four marks in the question.
Name the side the auxin collects on; 'uneven' on its own does not show the direction.
parts.workedSolution: Auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot and moves down it. Light entering from the left makes the auxin unevenly distributed, so more of it ends up on the shaded right-hand side. Auxin causes cells to elongate, so the cells on the right side become longer than those on the left. One side longer than the other makes the shoot curve to the left, towards the light.

pattern.regex: more (auxin )?on the (lit|light|left)[^;\n]{0,20}side|auxin (moves|goes|travels|collects|gathers|builds up|is pulled|is attracted|is drawn)[^;\n]{0,15}towards the light

commonErrors.feedback: Auxin collects on the side away from the light. If it collected on the lit side, that side would grow longer and the shoot would lean away from the light.

parts.stem:
Three shoots were left whole and lit from the right for 48 hours. Their angles of curvature were 31°, 29°, 33°.
Calculate the mean angle of curvature.
Show your working out.

scheme.for: adds the three angles: 31 + 29 + 33 = 93
divides by 3 to give 31 (degrees)
scheme.examinerNote: ecf from an arithmetic slip in the first point.

hints: Add first, then divide. Brackets on the calculator.

commonErrors.feedback: Typed without brackets, the calculator divides only the last reading before adding. Put the whole sum in brackets: the mean must lie between your smallest and largest reading.

parts.stem:
Shoot C had a black cap over its tip and gave a mean of 1°. Shoot E had a black collar around the stem below the tip and gave a mean of 32°.
Explain what these two results show about where a shoot detects light.

accepted: shoot E, with a collar round the stem below the tip, still curved by 32 degrees, but shoot C, with a black cap over the tip, hardly curved at all, so the tip is the part of the shoot that detects the light

scheme.for: shoot E still curved (32°, close to the whole shoot's 31°), so covering the stem makes no difference
shoot C barely curved (1°), so covering the tip stops the response
therefore the tip is the part that detects the light

hints: Quote both figures before you draw the conclusion.
One treatment differs from the whole shoot by one change only.
parts.workedSolution: Shoot E, with the stem below the tip covered, still curved by 32°, almost the same as the 31° of a whole shoot, so covering the stem makes no difference. Shoot C, with the tip covered, curved by only 1°. The part that must be exposed to light is therefore the tip, so the tip is where the light is detected.

commonErrors.feedback: The explanation needs the figures. Quote both means and then say what they show.

parts.stem: Shoot B had its tip cut off. State two things that were true of shoot B after 48 hours.

accepted: it did not bend, and it did not grow because there was no tip to produce auxin

scheme.for: it did not bend / stayed straight
it did not grow (no tip, so no auxin)
scheme.examinerNote: Summer 2025 B1 H Q4(b): most stated no tip or no auxin, but fewer went on to say there was no growth.

hints: Two things, so two separate statements.
The tip does two jobs: it detects light and it makes the auxin that drives growth.
parts.workedSolution: Shoot B stayed straight and it did not grow, because with the tip removed there was no auxin to make the cells elongate.

commonErrors.feedback: Half the answer is there. The tip also supplies the auxin that makes cells elongate, so with it removed the shoot does not grow at all.

context.setting: Cells measured down each side of one bending shoot

parts.stem:
Cells down the shaded side of a shoot grew from a mean length of 100 µm to 145 µm in 48 hours.
Calculate the percentage increase in cell length.
Show your working out.

scheme.for: finds the increase: 145 − 100 = 45
divides by the ORIGINAL length and multiplies by 100: 45 ÷ 100 × 100
scheme.examinerNote: March 2026 B1 H Q7(b): some divided by the incorrect denominator and gained only partial credit.
ecf through from an error in the subtraction.

hints: Percentage increase = increase ÷ starting value × 100.
The starting value is the one before the change, not the one after.

commonErrors.feedback: Divided by the final length instead of the starting length. 45 ÷ 145 × 100 gives 31.0%; the denominator is always the value you started from.

parts.stem:
Cells down the lit side of the same shoot increased by 10% over the same 48 hours.
Explain how these two figures account for the shape of the shoot.

accepted: the shaded side grew by 45% and the lit side by only 10%, because there is more auxin on the shaded side making its cells elongate more, so that side becomes longer and the shoot curves towards the light

scheme.for: the shaded side grew much more than the lit side (45% against 10%, a difference of 35 percentage points)
because there is more auxin on the shaded side, which makes its cells elongate more
one side longer than the other makes the shoot curve towards the light
reject: the shoot moves towards the light

hints: Compare the two figures first, using both numbers.
Then name the hormone, then say what the difference in length does to the shape.
parts.workedSolution: The shaded side's cells increased by 45% while the lit side's increased by only 10%, a difference of 35 percentage points. There is more auxin on the shaded side, and auxin makes cells elongate, so the shaded side becomes longer than the lit side. A stem that is longer down one side must curve, and it curves towards the light.

commonErrors.feedback: A plant does not want or look for anything. Describe the growth: more auxin, longer cells on one side, so the shoot curves.

context.setting: A tracer count of auxin on the two sides of a shoot tip

parts.stem:
A shoot tip was lit from one side. Of 240 units of auxin measured, 156 units were on one side.
Calculate the percentage of the auxin on that side.
hints: Part over whole, times 100.

commonErrors.feedback: Divided by the other side instead of the total. The whole is 240 units, so the calculation is 156 ÷ 240 × 100.

parts.stem: State which side of the shoot the 65% was on, and give a reason.

accepted: the shaded side, because light makes the auxin move away from the lit side so most of it collects on the side away from the light

scheme.for: the shaded side / the side away from the light
because light causes the auxin to be unevenly distributed, collecting away from the light

hints: More auxin where there is less light.
parts.workedSolution: The 65% was on the shaded side. One-sided light makes the auxin unevenly distributed, with more of it collecting on the side away from the light, which is why that side elongates more.

pattern.regex: ^(?![^]*(shaded|away from the light|dark side|unlit|less light))[^]*(lit side|light side|facing the light|towards the lamp)

commonErrors.feedback: Auxin collects away from the light. If it gathered on the lit side, that side would grow longer and the shoot would bend away from the light.

context.setting: A houseplant that has to be turned round every week

parts.stem:
A houseplant stands beside a window. After two weeks its stems all lean towards the glass.
Describe what has happened to the stems.

accepted: the stems have grown towards the light, because the cells on the side away from the window grew longer than those facing it

scheme.for: the stems have grown / bent towards the light or window
because the cells on the shaded side grew longer than those on the lit side

hints: Say which way, then say what made that shape.
parts.workedSolution: The stems have grown towards the window. The cells on the side away from the window elongated more than those facing it, so each stem curves towards the light.

commonErrors.feedback: Describe the growth rather than a purpose. One side's cells got longer, which bends the stem towards the light.

parts.stem: Suggest why turning the pot round by a half turn every week keeps the plant upright.

accepted: turning the pot puts the other side towards the light, so the side that used to be shaded now faces the light and the two sides end up growing by about the same amount

scheme.for: turning it puts the previously shaded side towards the light
so over time both sides elongate by about the same amount and the stem stays straight

hints: Which side is shaded after the turn?
parts.workedSolution: After the half turn the side that was shaded faces the window and the side that was lit is now shaded. Over several weeks each side spends about the same time shaded, so each elongates by about the same amount and the stem stays upright.

parts.stem:
A student plans to cover the tips of some shoots with black caps and leave others uncovered.
Suggest why the investigation also needs a set of shoots with clear caps over their tips.

accepted: the clear cap is a control that lets light through, so if those shoots still bend it shows the bending is stopped by the lack of light and not by the weight or presence of the cap itself

scheme.for: it acts as a control
it shows that any effect is caused by the light being blocked, not by having a cap on the tip

hints: Ask what else changes when you put a black cap on a shoot.
A control changes everything except the one factor being tested.
parts.workedSolution: The clear cap is a control: it blocks nothing but is the same size and weight as the black one. If the clear-capped shoots still bend, the only difference that matters is the light being blocked, so the black cap's effect cannot be blamed on having a cap at all.

commonErrors.feedback: A control is not a repeat. Its job here is to show that it is the blocking of light, and not the cap itself, that stops the bending.

parts.stem:
The student measures three shoots in each group rather than one.
Explain what this improves, and name one thing it does not improve.

accepted: measuring three shoots and taking a mean improves the reliability of the results because an odd shoot shows up as an anomaly, but it does not improve the accuracy, which depends on how well the angle is measured

scheme.for: improves reliability
because a mean can be taken and an anomalous shoot can be spotted
it does not improve accuracy, which depends on how the angle is measured
scheme.examinerNote: Repeating is the standard reliability answer; 'to improve accuracy' is the standard wrong reason.

hints: Reliability and accuracy are different things.
What would make the measured angle itself closer to the true value?
parts.workedSolution: Three shoots per group let the student calculate a mean and spot any shoot that behaves very differently from the others, so the results are more reliable. It does not make them more accurate: accuracy depends on how carefully the angle of curvature is measured, which repeating does not change.

commonErrors.feedback: Repeating improves reliability, not accuracy. Accuracy is about how close a single measurement is to the true value, and that depends on the measuring, not the number of repeats.

Describe and explain what has happened, using the hormone auxin.

indicativeContent.point: auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot
the one-sided light makes the auxin unevenly distributed
there is more auxin on the shaded side than on the lit side
auxin causes the cells to elongate
the shaded side therefore grows longer than the lit side
so the shoot bends towards the light, which is differential growth

scheme.for: banded: count the indicative points present, then place within the band on the quality of written communication — Band A [5]-[6] five or six points, Band B [3]-[4] three or four, Band C [1]-[2] one or two, [0] response not worthy of credit
scheme.examinerNote: A point contradicted elsewhere in the answer is not counted. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Name the process and the hormone first: two easy points before the mechanism.
Then walk the four bullets in order — made at the tip, moves down, uneven, elongation.
parts.workedSolution: The response is called phototropism and the hormone responsible is auxin. Auxin is produced at the tip of each shoot and moves down the shoot. Because light reaches the tray from one side only, the auxin becomes unevenly distributed, with more of it on the shaded side than on the side facing the window. Auxin causes cells to elongate, so the cells on the shaded side become longer than those on the lit side. This differential growth makes each shoot curve towards the window, which is why the whole tray leans the same way.

commonErrors.feedback: The specification's word is elongation: the same cells become longer. Cell division would make the shoot thicker, not curved.
More auxin ends up on the shaded side. Put it on the lit side and your own explanation predicts a shoot leaning away from the window.

findTheMistake.stem:
Orla is asked: 'Explain how auxin causes a shoot to bend towards light coming from the left. [4]'
Her answer:
studentWorking: Auxin is made at the tip of the shoot.
The auxin moves down the shoot.
The light makes more auxin collect on the left side, facing the light.
That side then makes more cells, so the shoot bends to the left.
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Auxin collects on the side **away from** the light, not the side facing it. Line 3 has it the wrong way round, and line 4 then has to be wrong too: if the lit side grew longer, the shoot would lean **away** from the light. Line 4 also says **more cells**, when auxin causes the existing cells to **elongate**.
correction: Auxin is made at the tip of the shoot.
The auxin moves down the shoot.
The light makes more auxin collect on the right side, away from the light.
Auxin makes those cells elongate, so the right side grows longer and the shoot bends to the left, towards the light.
findTheMistake.feedback: Two marks from four, and the two you have are the two most people get. The fix is a single sentence to memorise: **more auxin where there is less light**. Check it against the picture every time — the long cells have to be on the outside of the curve, which is the shaded side. Then swap 'more cells' for 'elongate', because that is the word the scheme lists.

prompts.answer: The growth of a stem towards light: differential growth of cells caused by an uneven distribution of auxin in response to light coming from one direction.

prompts.prompt: Name the plant hormone that causes phototropism.
Give the four stages of phototropism in order (Higher).
prompts.answer: Auxin is produced at the tip of the shoot; it moves down the shoot; light causes an uneven distribution, with more auxin on the shaded side; auxin causes cell elongation, so the shaded side grows longer and the shoot bends towards the light.

prompts.prompt: Which side of a shoot has more auxin, and why does that make it bend towards the light?
prompts.answer: The shaded side. Auxin makes cells elongate, so the shaded side grows longer than the lit side, and a stem that is longer on one side curves towards the other — towards the light.

prompts.prompt: Does auxin make cells divide or make them longer?
prompts.answer: Longer. Auxin causes cell elongation. Writing 'more cells' or 'the cells divide' describes cell division and does not earn the elongation mark.

prompts.prompt: A shoot has its tip cut off and is then lit from one side. What two things happen?

prompts.prompt: Why is 'the shoot moves towards the light' not enough for the mark?
prompts.answer: A tropism is growth, not movement, and the mark scheme wants a direction. Write that the shoot bends or grows towards the light.

prompts.prompt: How do you calculate a percentage increase?
prompts.answer: Increase divided by the ORIGINAL value, multiplied by 100. Dividing by the final value is the error examiners report most often on these questions.
